lesson_title: The Stubborn Cow: How Contour Lines Find the River
hook_text: A cow that refuses to climb can find every river on a map.
clip_script: Picture one particularly stubborn cow who grazes only along her own level, at exactly 300 metres, never a step up or down. She ambles along the hillside until the ground ahead dips into a valley with a stream at the bottom. Straight across is forbidden — the middle of the dip is below her level. So she turns into the valley, follows her height along its side, steps across the stream at the one point where the far bank returns to 300 metres, and ambles back out along the opposite side. Sketch her route from above: it is a V. The tip of the V is the deepest she went up the valley — always towards the higher ground the stream is arriving from. So the V points upstream, and the water slides out through the V's open mouth, downhill. Every contour crossing that valley repeats the same V, one after another, like arrowheads aimed at the source. That is how you find a river on a map with no blue line at all.
visual_style: A cartoon cow tracing a glowing level path around a 3D hillside, the path flattening into map view to reveal a chain of V-shaped contours, arrowheads lighting up towards the source.
mood: Charming and mischievous, snapping into a satisfying aha.
pacing: Amble with the cow through the detour, then a quick top-down snap and a rapid-fire close on the V rule.
call_to_action: Take the full lesson and read valleys, spurs and cliffs straight off the brown lines.
